bracket: [Textbook misprint in the stem: the piecewise function prints the SAME condition on both branches — \(= x^2 + \sin x + 1\) for \(x \le 0\) and \(= x^2 - 2x + 1\) for \(x \le 0\). As printed the function is doubly defined on \(x \le 0\) and undefined for \(x > 0\), so it cannot be what is intended; the second branch must read \(x > 0\). Under that reading both branches give \(1\) at \(x = 0\), so \(f\) is continuous there, while the left derivative \(2x + \cos x \to 1\) and the right derivative \(2x - 2 \to -2\) differ, so \(f\) is not differentiable — which is the keyed answer.]

[Textbook misprint in the stem, answer-affecting as printed: the radical bar overshoots to cover \(x + 2\). Measured on the page, the stem's vinculum spans 72 px, covering the \(x\), the \(+\) and the \(2\), against the same book's ordinary \(\sqrt{x}\) at 22 px elsewhere on the same page. As printed the derivative of \(\dfrac{x-4}{\sqrt{x+2}}\) is \(\dfrac{x+8}{2(x+2)^{3/2}}\), which matches NO option, so the question is unanswerable. The intended stem is \(\dfrac{x-4}{\sqrt{x}+2}\), which factors as \(\dfrac{\left(\sqrt{x}-2\right)\left(\sqrt{x}+2\right)}{\sqrt{x}+2} = \sqrt{x} - 2\) and differentiates to \(\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\) — the keyed option. The answer above follows the intended reading. Note the option set straddles both readings, which is presumably how the ambiguity arose.]
